scope: Theorem 1.1 (Height universality through the roughening threshold) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every admissible J, the threshold in Equation (1.3) satisfies 0 < βc(J) < ∞. The supremum there is finite when 0 < β < βc(J) and infinite when β ≥ βc(J), including equality. There are an integer L = L(J) ≥ 2 and a unique positive function βeff(J, β), defined for β ≥ βc(J), such that along the full sequence N → ∞ HN =⇒ s βeff(J, β) v2 J ΦT in H−3 (T2 ). (1.6) For every smooth real mean-zero f, lim N→∞ log EeHN (f) = βeff(J, β) 2v2 J (f, (−∆T)−1 f). (1.7) Furthermore, βeff(J, βc(J)) = 8πv2 J , (1.8) lim β↓βc(J) βeff(J, β) − βeff(J, βc(J)) β − βc(J) = +∞. (1.9) The function βeff(J, ·) is differentiable on (βc(J), ∞), and for some cJ > 0, βeff(J, β) = β + OJ (e−cJ β ) (β → ∞). (1.10) For Jρ = {x ∈ Z2 \ {0} : |x|∞ ≤ ρ}, βc(Jρ) 8πv2 Jρ −→ 1 (ρ → ∞). (1.11) In particular v2 Jnn = 1/4 and the nearest-neighbor effective temperature at roughening is 2π.
